title: Terraform upgrade canary + post-deploy smoke & model-load runner
creator: Ava Chou
description:
Summary:
We need an automated canary-oriented post-deploy verification runner that combines Terraform upgrade gating with API readiness checks, model load tests, and targeted smoke tests for VPC/private deployments. The goal is to provide an executable pipeline and runbook that: (1) validates Terraform plan/apply changes in a non-blocking canary slice, (2) performs API-level readiness probes, (3) loads representative model artifacts and measures model-init time and memory usage, and (4) runs synthetic traffic smoke tests to exercise batching, KV cache, and fallback logic.

Background and motivation:
- We've had incidents where upgrades to infra modules (subnet changes, SGs, IAM roles) succeeded but inference runtime warmup failed under production-like concurrency.
- Existing post-deploy checks focus on basic API L7 checks and simple model start hogs; they don't measure model warmup latency, KV cache effectiveness, or the failure modes for partial capacity (canary).
- This ticket builds a repeatable, Terraform-aware canary gating harness so upgrades can be safely rolled and automatically rolled back based on defined SLOs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A CI job (GitHub Actions) that runs after terraform apply for canary workspace. The job must:
  * Run API readiness probe against canary endpoint (health, /v1/status).
  * Spin up a model-load harness that pulls target model variant and records model init time, GPU mem at peak, and first-token latency.
  * Run a 3-minute synthetic smoke workload (mix of short chat, streaming, and embeddings) with configurable concurrency.
  * Calculate pass/fail using thresholds (see thresholds section).
- Runbook updated and linked in the ticket and console.
- Metrics emitted to telemetry with tag terraform.canary=<run-id> for traceability.
- Automatic Canary rollback hook: if failures detected, create issue and post a rollback instruction to the deploy channel.

Test plan and thresholds:
- API readiness: 99% of /v1/status responses must be HTTP 200 within 500ms.
- Model init time: first-token latency for model load must be < 6s for small-medium models, < 18s for large models.
- GPU memory: model peak memory must be within 95% of expected profile (reject if > 100% of profile).
- Error rate: synthetic workload must have < 0.5% HTTP 5xx and < 1% client-side timeouts over the 3-minute run.
- KV cache hit rate: must be >= 60% for workload with repeated prefixes (configurable).
- Canary pass requires all thresholds to be met; partial degradations trigger alert + manual review flow.

Automation design and components:
- Terraform gating: workspace 'canary' created per-PR, apply runs against a small subset of nodes (1-2 GPUs). Use terraform-plan-diff to identify surface-area changes and block if IAM/network changes are high-risk.
- Canary runner (go service + scripts) will:
  * Read terraform output to find canary endpoints and credentials.
  * Execute API readiness probes and start the model-load runner via remote executor (kubectl/ssh depending on deployment flavor).
  * Run distributed smoke clients from two AZs to exercise routing.
  * Push metrics to the telemetry pipeline with tags: run_id, terraform_change, commit_sha, canary_node_ids.
- Integration with deploy orchestration: the runner posts status back to the PR and to #deployments-canary Slack channel.
- Rollback hook: if canary fails, the pipeline flags the Terraform state and comments on the PR with a recommended rollback plan and links to a pre-populated revert PR template.

Runbook (high level steps):
1. Trigger: terraform apply on canary workspace completes.
2. CI job starts and invokes canary-runner with run_id.
3. Runner performs health checks and model-load probes sequentially.
4. Runner executes smoke workload, collects metrics.
5. Runner evaluates thresholds and posts PASS/FAIL.
6a. PASS -> mark canary as healthy and continue to staged rollout.
6b. FAIL -> create incident ticket, post recommended rollback, and mark terraform apply as requiring manual remediation.

Observability and dashboards:
- New dashboard 'vpc-canary/health' with panels: API p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-init histogram, GPU memory trend, KV cache hit rate.
- Alerts: trigger if API 5xx > 0.5% over 5m OR model-init > threshold OR GPU memory exceeds expected. Alert routes to oncall and #deployments-canary.

Artifacts and links:
- GH PR template for rollback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/placeholder
- Prototype runner repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canary-runner (proof-of-concept branch 'terraform-integration')
- Draft runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/VPC+Canary+Runbook
- Monitoring dashboard (WIP): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xxx/vpc-canary-health

Review feedback and decisions so far:
- Security reviewed minimal: runner will use short-lived credentials derived from terraform outputs; no long-lived keys in CI. (Security note: needs KMS review.)
- Design decision: run smoke clients from two AZs to catch cross-AZ routing issues.
- Trade-off: canary uses reduced node count to lower cost, but might mask scale-related failures; to mitigate we include a staged ramp to a small mid-size slice if canary passes.

Blocking issues and risks:
- Need infra team to expose terraform outputs in a secure way to the CI runner (blocking).
- KMS access pattern for retrieving model artifacts in private deployments requires security sign-off.
- Some legacy VPC templates don't support 'canary' subdivision; we may need to create a temporary override module.

Next steps and checklist:
- [ ] Finalize Terraform workspace naming convention and secrets retrieval path (owner: Infra).
- [ ] Land canary-runner minimal: health probe + model-load (owner: Diego). Target: 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Add metrics emitters and dashboards (owner: Observability).
- [ ] Security KMS sign-off (owner: Security).
- [ ] Draft CI job and PR comment connector (owner: CI).

Comments and updates:
- 2026-03-02 (Ava): Pushed initial spec to the canary-runner repo and stubbed the GH action.
- 2026-03-04 (Diego): Implemented API readiness probe and basic model-load script. Observed model-init ~7.2s for test-mini on canary nodes — slightly above target; investigating kernel launch overhead.
- 2026-03-08 (Maya R.): Security requested explicit KMS flow and short-lived role assumption; added to blockers.
- 2026-03-10 (Diego): Hooked metrics emitter to telemetry; created draft Grafana panels and added run_id tags.

Manual steps for oncall if canary fails:
- Run: ./scripts/canary-fallback --run-id=<id> to collect logs and model traces.
- Inspect: Grafana panels for GPU memory and model-init spikes.
- Rollback: revert the Terraform PR or apply previous state using terraform workspace rollback instructions linked in the runbook.

Notes for implementers:
- Be conservative in thresholds for initial rollout; prefer manual inspection for first 3 production runbooks.
- All code must include telemetry tags: terraform.change, commit.sha, run_id.
- Keep the runner lightweight; it should orchestrate remote probes rather than re-implementing full load generators inside the runner process.

Related tickets referenced in dependencies: ENG-30142 (deploy orchestrator), ENG-213456 (terraform module integrity).
